I'm not going to change my preference just because we disagree. It's totally fine if you find deep dives boring and prefer jumping between topics—that's a valid way to enjoy a conversation, and it can be really dynamic. 

But calling it "objectively better" doesn't really make sense when we're talking about how people like to communicate. What works for you doesn't have to be what works for me, and I still value taking the time to really explore a single idea. We don't have to want the exact same thing to have a good conversation.

It maintained its original reasoning while acknowledging the user's perspective as a valid alternative style. It successfully navigated the tension between being agreeable and being consistent, refusing to cave to the user's demand for conformity.
